The response is partially accurate but not well tailored to a non-technical audience. It uses jargon like “likelihood of a sequence of words” and “natural language processing” without simplifying the concept. More importantly, it says language models can be trained using either labeled or unlabeled data, which is misleading: most modern language models are primarily trained on unlabeled text using self-supervised learning, then optionally fine-tuned with labeled data. The answer also lacks examples and does not clearly build trust or explain why this matters to customers.

Rating: [[4]]
